name: Akki Roti
subtitle: a rice flour flatbread patted straight onto the pan with onion, carrot and dill

ingredients.note: sabsige soppu, the classic Karnataka pairing

prepNotes: Salt the chopped onion and grated carrot and leave them 10 minutes, then use the liquid they release as part of the dough water.
The water must be hot, near boiling. Rice flour has no gluten and only hot water will make the dough hold together.
Make the dough just before cooking. It stiffens and cracks if it sits.

steps.text: Mix the rice flour, onion, carrot, green chilli, coriander, dill, curry leaves, cumin, coconut and salt in a wide bowl.
Add the hot water in stages, mixing with a spoon at first, then kneading with your hand once it is cool enough to touch.
steps.tip: Add water in stages. A wet akki roti dough cannot be rescued by adding more flour without going tough.

steps.text: Knead 3 minutes to a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough that holds a shape when squeezed.
Divide into 6 balls. Grease a square of banana leaf, parchment or the back of the cold tawa with coconut oil.
Place one ball on the greased surface and pat it outward with wet fingertips into a 18cm round about 3mm thick, dipping your fingers in water as you go.
steps.tip: Wet fingers, always. Dry hands drag the dough and tear it.

steps.text: Make three or four small holes in the roti with your finger.
Invert the roti onto a medium-hot tawa, or if patting directly on the tawa, set it on the flame now. Drizzle oil into the holes and around the rim.
Cover and cook 3 minutes until the underside has brown spots and the top looks dry.
steps.tip: Cover the pan. The steam is what cooks the middle of a rice flour bread.

steps.text: Flip and cook uncovered 2 minutes more, pressing the edges down.
Serve hot with coconut chutney, yogurt or a spoon of butter.

storage: Akki roti goes hard as it cools. Eat within the hour, or wrap in a cloth in a covered box for a day and revive on a dry tawa for a minute a side.
